extracted.intended_audience: general readers (Wikipedia readers) and researchers/journalists seeking a comprehensive overview of COVID-19 misinformation and responses
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive, encyclopedic compilation of claims, fact-checks, official guidance, platform and government responses, and consequences related to COVID-19 misinformation and disinformation worldwide. Used to inform news coverage, research, and public information efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHO advises that ivermectin only be used to treat COVID-19 within clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: "WHO advises that ivermectin only be used to treat COVID-19 within clinical trials". (Newsroom. World Health Organization. Geneva, Switzerland. 31 March 2021)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official WHO guidance limiting ivermectin use to clinical-trial contexts; included as authoritative source discouraging routine use outside trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMA advises against use of ivermectin outside randomized clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: “EMA advises against use of ivermectin for the prevention or treatment of COVID-19 outside randomised clinical trials". (European Medicines Agency. Amsterdam. 22 March 2021)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory advice from the European Medicines Agency recommending against off-label or non-trial use of ivermectin for COVID-19.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA consumer guidance: do not use ivermectin to treat or prevent COVID-19
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why You Should Not Use Ivermectin to Treat or Prevent COVID-19". (United States Food and Drug Administration. Consumer Updates. 10 December 2021)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA consumer-directed warning against using veterinary or non-prescribed ivermectin for COVID-19, intended as public-safety guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional society guidance on ivermectin (IDSA/NIH statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: "IDSA Guidelines on the Treatment and Management of Patients with COVID-19: Recommendations 23-24: Ivermectin" and statements that NIH found "insufficient data to recommend for or against its use outside the context of a clinical trial."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical-practice and research-oriented guidance from professional bodies (IDSA) and NIH stressing insufficient evidence and restricting ivermectin use to trials or research settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open sharing of COVID-19 research data and findings
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sharing research data and findings relevant to the novel coronavirus (COVID-19) outbreak". (wellcome.ac.uk press release. 31 January 2020)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wellcome and similar calls/press releases urging researchers and publishers to share data and findings relevant to COVID-19 openly and rapidly to support response and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove paywalls for coronavirus coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: "Major Publishers Take Down Paywalls for Coronavirus Coverage" (reporting that major publishers removed paywalls for COVID-19 reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/publishing practice during a public-health emergency: make reporting and research on COVID-19 accessible by lifting paywalls to enable broad public and professional access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platforms should remove posts spreading coronavirus misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: "As coronavirus misinformation spreads on social media, Facebook removes posts"; "Facebook says it has taken down 7 million posts for spreading coronavirus misinformation".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content-moderation expectation that major platforms actively remove or restrict demonstrably false/misleading COVID-19 claims and content as part of countering the 'infodemic'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketplaces and retailers remove fake or dangerous COVID-19 products
rubrics_metrics.description: "Amazon culls one million fake coronavirus products"; FDA warning letters and criminal actions against sellers of fake 'miracle' cures (e.g., Genesis 2 Church, sellers of toxic bleach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer-protection practice: online marketplaces and regulators should remove/act against fraudulent or dangerous products marketed as COVID-19 cures or preventives, and enforcement actions (warnings, prosecutions) are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking and debunking of COVID-19 claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous fact-check examples cited (AFP Fact Check, Snopes, Reuters, AP, fact-checking of specific claims such as spraying disinfectant, cabbage warnings, helicopter spraying, vaccine/scam claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic and civil-society role: systematically verify and debunk false or misleading COVID-19 claims, publishing clear corrections and evidence-based explanations to counter misinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer warnings and safety guidance from regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: "COVID-19 Consumer Warnings and Safety Tips" (Federal Communications Commission), "Coronavirus Advice for Consumers" (Federal Trade Commission), and other consumer-facing advisories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory agencies provide explicit consumer warnings (scam alerts, safety tips) aimed at protecting the public from fraud, scams, and harmful 'remedies' during the pandemic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain research integrity; retract flawed COVID-19 papers
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'Retracted coronavirus (COVID-19) papers' (Retraction Watch) and analyses of retractions and 'citation pollution'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly standard: journals, researchers, and readers should monitor and correct the literature (retractions, notices) and be aware of the harms of fast/poorly vetted publications and meta-analyses based on flawed or summary-level data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tackle the 'infodemic' while avoiding stigmatization
rubrics_metrics.description: "Coronavirus: UN health agency moves fast to tackle 'infodemic'; Guterres warns against stigmatization".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-health communication standard: actively counter misinformation ('infodemic') while ensuring messaging does not stigmatize groups or individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration between health agencies and knowledge platforms to combat misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage noting cooperation such as 'Wikipedia and W.H.O. Join to Combat Covid-19 Misinformation' and reporting on how Wikipedia prevents spread of coronavirus misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-sector collaboration expectation: health authorities and major information platforms/knowledge projects should coordinate to ensure accurate, accessible, and up-to-date public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governments' use of misinformation laws and enforcement (arrests and legal action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple reports documenting arrests, prosecutions, and legal action for spreading COVID-19 'fake news' (e.g., Iran, Cambodia, Morocco, Vietnam, Nigeria, Pakistan, Myanmar, Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive standard: many jurisdictions used criminal or administrative measures against 'fake news' during the pandemic; coverage highlights the tension between misinformation enforcement and freedom of expression/human-rights concerns.
